**Solution 1 has the right method but a factorization error. None of the three final answers is correct.**

**Factorization:** 1260 = 2²·3²·5·7 (since 4·9·35 = 1260), so 1260² = 2⁴·3⁴·5²·7². Solution 1 wrote 1260 = 2³·3²·5·7, which is 2520, and so used 2⁶ instead of 2⁴.

**Method check:** Scanning a uniformly random permutation of the divisors and skipping erased elements gives the same distribution as the process. A divisor d is picked exactly when it is the first element of its up-set {m : d | m, m | N} to appear. So P(d is picked) = 1/|up-set(d)|, and E[T] = Σ_d 1/|up-set(d)|. For N = ∏ p_i^{a_i}, this factors as ∏ H_{a_i+1}. I checked this on the divisor diamond of pq, which gives 9/4 by direct enumeration.

**Correct value:** With a = (4, 4, 2, 2),

E[T] = H₅² · H₃² = (137/60)² · (11/6)² = 2271049/129600 ≈ 17.52.

**Other solutions:**
- **Solution 2** assumes the picks are a uniform random ordering of all 225 divisors. The process stops early, so this is wrong. It gives 113, which is far too small.
- **Solution 3** conjectures E[T] = H_N from examples. Its diamond calculation gives 25/12, but the true value is 9/4, so the conjecture is false. Its diamond step also drops the pick itself from the count.

Solution 1 is the only one with the correct structure, so it is the closest, even though its final answer 2005517/100800 is wrong because of the exponent error.

CHOICE: 1
